Hi, thank you for your report and the detailed diagnosis! Yeah, I don't think that integer scaling gets tested much unfortunately.

> [This commit](https://github.com/wmww/godot/commit/7e59c52c80ce36c2a1187661e1d2c5e26610176c) seems to fix my issue by always using the fractional scaling code path when the viewporter protocol is available. However this doesn't solve the underlying issue, so it could still be hit with compositors that don't support the protocol.

Indeed, integer scaling itself must work. I'd keep the preference as is and not always use fractional scaling if available for now.

> Also it's claudeslop, so it could be wrong in other subtle ways.

I'd avoid the use of LLMs as the `WaylandThread` interface is already pretty complex for humans ;)

> Happy to open a PR with it, or to human-write a better solution with guidance on how to go about that (I'm experienced with Wayland, less so with Godot's windowing code and thread safety model).

Thank you! No worries, with all the data you collected I think I can make a quick fix right now. I'll let you know how it goes.

> Seems like a separate and mostly harmless bug, but worth fixing at the same time.

I'll also address this, thank you :D

Uh. It looks like on my setup sway 1.11 (just like yours) buffer scaling never happens. That's interesting.

The only way I found to trigger it was to hide the fractional scaling global outright with [`wl-veil`](https://github.com/mahkoh/wl-proxy/tree/master/apps/wl-veil):

```
WAYLAND_DEBUG=1 wl-veil -f fractional-scale-v1 bin/godot.linuxbsd.editor.dev.x86_64 2>&1 | grep buffer_scale
```

I see some quirky behavior I didn't see before but I still can't easily replicate the crash.

Hi, PR #116692 is up! Please give it a spin :D

Note that it's a PoC but hopefully does the job. If it works I'll make it pretty.

> I see some quirky behavior

Welp, turns out that it's libdecor. That'll be a can of worms for another time :P
